title_en: Li Weixiang v. Li Gemei — dispute over inheritance rights
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 15 of the Rural Land Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, where rural land is contracted by households, the contractor is the farmer household of the collective economic organization, and its essential characteristic is that rural land contract management is carried out with the farmer household within the collective economic organization as the unit. The right to rural land contract management under the household contract belongs to the farmer household, not to any individual member. According to Article 3 of the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China, estate is the lawful personal property left by a citizen at death. The right to rural land contract management is not personal property, and therefore no inheritance issue arises. For household contracts except for forest land, when one or several members of the farmer household contracting agricultural land die, the contract management is still conducted on a household basis, and the contracted land shall continue to be contract-managed by the other family members of the said household. When all members of the farmer household engaged in contract management die, since the acquisition of the contract management right is based on collective membership, the land contract management right becomes extinguished and cannot be continued by the heirs of the members of the farmer household, nor can it be treated as the estate of the members of the farmer household.

full_text_en:
Li Weixiang v. Li Gemei — Dispute over Inheritance Rights

【Ruling Summary】

According to Article 15 of the Rural Land Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, where a rural land is contracted on a household basis, the contractor is the household of the relevant collective economic organization, and the essential characteristic of such a contract is that the rural land contracting and management are carried out on the basis of the household unit within the collective economic organization. The right to the contracted management of rural land under the household contract method belongs to the household, not to any individual member of the household. According to Article 3 of the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China, the estate is the lawful personal property left by a citizen at the time of his death. The right to the contracted management of rural land is not personal property, and therefore no issue of inheritance arises. For household contracts other than those for forestland, when one or several members of the household that contracted the agricultural land die, the contracted management continues on the basis of the household, and the contracted land continues to be managed by the other members of that household; when all members of the household that contracted the management die, because the acquisition of the contracted management right is based on collective membership, the right to the contracted management of the land is extinguished, and it cannot be continued by the heirs of the deceased household members, nor can it be treated as the estate of those household members.

Plaintiff: Li Weixiang, male, 41 years old, Han nationality, residing in Sijia Community, Jiangning Subdistrict, Jiangning District, Nanjing City.

Defendant: Li Gemei, female, 43 years old, Han nationality, residing in Sijia Community, Jiangning Subdistrict, Jiangning District, Nanjing City.

The plaintiff, Li Weixiang, filed a lawsuit with the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant, Li Gemei, over a dispute concerning inheritance rights.

The plaintiff, Li Weixiang, alleged: The plaintiff and the defendant, Li Gemei, are siblings. On February 13, 1998, the plaintiff's father, Li Shengyun, subcontracted 3.08 mu of his contracted farmland to Rui Guoning, a fellow villager. Because Li Shengyun was illiterate, the subcontract was signed by Li Gemei on his behalf. Later, Li Shengyun died in 2004. Before his death, he gave the contract certificate for the said 3.08 mu of agricultural land to the plaintiff and stated that the 3.08 mu of land should be jointly inherited by the plaintiff and Li Gemei, each taking half. However, Li Gemei has been taking possession of the entire 3.08 mu of land. The plaintiff has negotiated with Li Gemei many times, but Li Gemei has refused to return it. The plaintiff requests the court to rule that the plaintiff has the inheritance right to 1.54 mu of the 3.08 mu of land, and to order the defendant to deliver that portion of the land to the plaintiff.

The defendant, Li Gemei, argued: The disputed land should be entirely contracted and managed by the defendant. The reasons are: (1) The plaintiff, Li Weixiang, has a non-agricultural household registration and should not enjoy the right to contracted management of rural land; (2) Both parents of the plaintiff and defendant passed away more than two years ago, and the plaintiff's lawsuit has exceeded the statute of limitations; (3) The defendant's household has more members than the plaintiff's household, and therefore the parents gave the disputed land to the defendant for cultivation; (4) The plaintiff performed less duty of support for the parents, while the defendant performed more, and therefore the defendant should have a larger share of the inheritance of the right to contract the disputed land.

The Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City found the following facts at the first instance:

The defendant, Li Gemei, and the plaintiff, Li Weixiang, are siblings. At the time of the first round of household contracting of rural land, the plaintiff, the defendant, their father Li Shengyun, and their mother Zhou Guixiang lived together. At that time, Li Shengyun's household obtained the right to contracted management of 6.68 mu of land. Thereafter, Li Gemei and Li Weixiang married and formed their own households. By the time of the second round of household contracting of rural land in 1995, the local rural collective economic organization reallocated the contracted management rights for the original 6.68 mu of land of Li Shengyun's household. Li Weixiang's household obtained the right to contracted management of 1.8 mu of land, Li Gemei's household obtained the right to contracted management of 3.34 mu of land, and Li Shengyun's household obtained the right to contracted management of 1.54 mu of land. All three households received corresponding certificates for the right to contracted management. In February 1998, Li Shengyun transferred his contracted 1.54 mu of land to a fellow villager, Rui Guoning, for operation, and the transfer agreement was signed by Li Gemei on his behalf. Li Shengyun and Zhou Guixiang passed away successively on November 3, 2004, and April 4, 2005. Thereafter, the income from the transfer of the 1.54 mu of land originally contracted by Li Shengyun's household was taken by Li Gemei.

The issue in dispute in this case is whether the right to contracted management of rural land under the household contract method can be inherited.

The Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City held at the first instance:

According to Paragraph 2 of Article 3 of the Rural Land Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Rural Land Contract Law), rural land contracting adopts the household contract method within the rural collective economic organization. For rural land such as barren mountains, barren gullies, barren hills, and barren beaches that are not suitable for the household contract method, contracting may be conducted through bidding, auction, open negotiation, and other methods. Therefore, the right to contracted management of rural land in China is divided into two types: household contracts and contracts by other methods.

The main purpose of implementing the contracted management of rural land under the household contract method is to provide basic living security for each member of the rural collective economic organization. According to Article 15 of the Rural Land Contract Law, under the household contract method, the contractor is the household of the collective economic organization, and its essential characteristic is that the rural land contracting and management are carried out on the basis of the household unit within the collective economic organization. Consequently, this form of right to contracted management of rural land can only belong to the household, not to any individual member of the household. According to Article 3 of the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Inheritance Law), an estate is the lawful personal property left by a citizen at the time of his death. The right to contracted management of rural land is not personal property, and therefore no issue of inheritance arises.

For forestland contracts under household contracts and contracts for "four wasteland" land under other methods, due to the special nature of the land, the long investment cycle, slow returns, and long income period, in order to maintain the long-term stability of the contract, protect the interests of the contractor, and maintain social stability, according to Paragraph 2 of Article 31 and Article 50 of the Rural Land Contract Law, if the contractor of a forestland contract dies, his heirs may continue the contract within the contract period. If the contractor under a contract by other methods dies, his heirs may also continue the contract within the contract period. However, the continuation of the contract by the heir is not equivalent to inheritance as defined in the Inheritance Law. For household contracts other than those for forestland, the law does not grant the heir the right to continue the contract. When one or several members of the household that contracted the agricultural land die, the contracted management continues on the basis of the household, and the contracted land continues to be managed by the other members of that household; when all members of the household that contracted the management die, because the acquisition of the contracted management right is based on collective membership, the right to the contracted management of the land is extinguished, and the agricultural land should be taken back by the rural collective economic organization for redistribution, and cannot be continued by the heirs of the deceased household members. Otherwise, it would harm the rights and interests of other members of the collective economic organization and have a negative impact on the social security function of agricultural land.

In this case, the right to contracted management of the disputed land belongs to Li Shengyun's household, which is a household contract method, and the disputed land is not forestland. Therefore, after the death of Li Shengyun and his wife, the disputed land should be taken back by the local rural collective economic organization for redistribution, and cannot be continued by the heirs of Li Shengyun and his wife, nor can the right to contract the disputed agricultural land be treated as the estate of Li Shengyun and his wife.

Although Li Shengyun and Zhou Guixiang were the parents of the plaintiff Li Weixiang and the defendant Li Gemei, both Li Weixiang and Li Gemei had formed their own households after marriage. At the time of the second round of household contracting of rural land, Li Shengyun's household, Li Weixiang's household, and Li Gemei's household each obtained the right to contracted management of land and corresponding certificates for the right to contracted management. At that point, Li Weixiang and Li Gemei were no longer members of Li Shengyun's contracted land household, but were three independent contracted land households. Li Shengyun and his wife have both passed away, and there is no one to continue the contract for that household. The right to contracted management of the 1.54 mu of land left after the death of Li Shengyun and his wife should be taken back by the granter of the land. According to Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, a third party who does not have an independent claim to the subject matter of the litigation but has a legal interest in the outcome of the case may apply to participate in the proceedings, or the people's court may notify him to participate. During the trial of this case, the court notified the granter of the contract to participate in the proceedings and explained the relevant rights and obligations to the granter, but the granter explicitly stated that it would not participate in the proceedings. Based on the principle of "no trial without complaint," the court in this case does not address the issue of the ownership of the right to contracted management of the disputed land. Although Li Weixiang and Li Gemei are the children of Li Shengyun and his wife, each of their households has already obtained the corresponding right to contracted management of land. Therefore, neither Li Weixiang nor Li Gemei meets the statutory conditions for continuing the contract for the right to contracted management of the land left after the death of their parents. Consequently, Li Weixiang's claim for the return of the disputed land by Li Gemei is dismissed.

Accordingly, the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing City, in accordance with Paragraph 1 of Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 9, 15, 31, and 50 of the Rural Land Contract Law, rendered the following judgment on May 13, 2009:

All claims of the plaintiff Li Weixiang are dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither party filed an appeal within the statutory period, and the first-instance judgment has become legally effective.
